iPhone Duo will begin accepting pre-orders on Friday (October 16), but scammers are attempting to lure people to fake websites to place orders early.

The malware-laden website looks nearly identical to the real one and claims to offer a $500 discount coupon under the name of an 'authorized partner exclusive'...

Security researchers at Malwarebytes pointed out that the webpage uses the DarkSword exploit chain, which can target some older iPhones that have not been updated in time. Users don't need to do anything; simply visiting the webpage is enough to trigger the attack.

If the attack succeeds, the scammers will obtain your device identification data and status, and attempt to transmit the list of installed applications and the contents of your Apple Notes. Once completed, they will shift their target to your cryptocurrency wallet.

Afterwards, they will further attempt to access your messages, contacts, call history, voicemail, emails, calendar entries, and cached location data. The malware can also contact its server to obtain further instructions.

Google publicly disclosed this exploit chain as early as March this year, and Apple also released a patch later that same month.

9to5Mac Perspective

The usual precautionary advice still applies. Don't click on unknown links at will, unless you trust the sender and genuinely expect to receive such a link. Be sure to install iOS updates as soon as they are released.
